content.comment_body: On the new [product_name] [article_no], there are display options that differ from the older [article_no] model. When entering counter parameters, the display shows texts like '1+R' or '1-R' at the top right. I understand 'R' relates to retentivity but would like to know the significance of '1' and the meaning behind the '+' or '-' signs. Thanks again. [user_name]

Hello, Do you mean on the actual [product_name] display itself? With the [product_name] [version_no], you can set reference points for the on and off threshold limits, which might be what those symbols represent on your display. I'm not entirely certain, as I haven't programmed directly on the device itself since using [product_name] [version_no]. Regards,
Thank you [user_name]. I'm referring specifically to the '1' and the '+' sign in the attached diagram that indicates '1+R' and '2+R'. Thanks.

Hi there, Please refer to page 102 of the relevant [document] for more details. The three characters, such as '1+R', represent: 1 - parameter page number (some screens may show 2) + - parameter protection mode (+ or -) R - retentive value (R or /) Greetings.
Thanks [user_name]. I thought I reviewed the entire manual, but I must have missed that section.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking to understand the meaning of new symbols and representations introduced in the parameter display of the updated [product_name] hardware. Their main concern involves deciphering how these symbols relate to device functions and programming. While users consult supporting documentation, finding and interpreting new features is sometimes challenging.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward and easy-to-find explanations of new parameter symbols and display elements, both within the device interface and in the supporting documentation.
